user.created: A person was added to the organization, by an administrator or over SCIM.
user.updated: SCIM changed a person's profile or status.
user.deleted: A person was deleted from the organization.
user.password_set: An administrator set a person's password, ending their sessions.
user.bulk_imported: A bulk import of people finished, with how many rows succeeded and failed.

auth.password_changed: A person changed their own password.

session.revoked: A session ended, with the reason; its tokens stop working.

token.claims_change: A person's roles changed, so their next access token carries different claims.

group.member_added: A person was added to a group.
group.member_removed: A person was removed from a group.

group_template.applied: A group template was applied, creating its groups.

domain.created: A domain was added for verification.

agent.resumed: A suspended AI agent was made active again.
agent.decommissioned: An AI agent was decommissioned for good.
agent.sponsor_transferred: A person's AI agents were given to another sponsor.
agent.kill_switch: Every active AI agent of the organization was suspended at once.

abac_policy.deleted: An attribute-based access policy was deleted.

siem.sink_created: A log stream to a SIEM was created.
siem.sink_updated: A log stream to a SIEM was enabled or disabled.
siem.sink_deleted: A log stream to a SIEM was deleted.

rate_limits.updated: The organization's rate limits were changed.
rate_limits.deleted: The organization's rate limits were reset to the defaults.

oidc.client_locked_out: An application was locked out after too many wrong secrets.

tenant.suspended: The organization was suspended, ending its sessions.
tenant.deleted: The organization was deleted, ending its sessions.

scopes.label: Scopes
scopes.notYours: You don't hold it, so you can't grant it
scopes.vaultAll: Reads every secret in the vault

shownOnce.key: Copy the key now. You won't see it again.
shownOnce.clientSecret: Copy the client secret now. You won't see it again.
shownOnce.secret: Copy the secret now. You won't see it again.
shownOnce.hashed: Qeet ID keeps only a hash of it, so nobody can see it again. Store it in your secret manager.
shownOnce.credential: Copy the credential now. You won't see it again.
shownOnce.credentialWhy: Qeet ID records that it issued it, not the credential itself. Give it to the person it is about.
shownOnce.signingSecret: Copy the signing secret now. You won't see it again.
shownOnce.signingSecretWhy: Your endpoint checks each delivery's X-Qeet-Signature with it. To get a new one, rotate it.

description.all: Everything that calls Qeet ID without a person signing in, and who answers for it.
description.key: Static keys for scripts and CI jobs. Each call sends one as Authorization: ApiKey …; a revoked key is refused from its next call.
description.identity: Services that trade a client secret for tokens that last minutes, at POST /v1/oauth/token.
description.agent: AI agents that act within their scopes, each sponsored by a person who answers for it. Their tokens last an hour at most.

search.all: Search by name, ID or scope
search.key: Search by name, prefix or scope
search.identity: Search by name, client ID or scope
search.agent: Search by name, ID, scope or sponsor

row.notRecorded: Qeet ID doesn’t record when these are used

actions.replaceHint: A new key with the same scopes; then revoke this one

confirm.revoke: Anything still sending this key is refused from its next call. It stays in the list as revoked and can’t be turned back on.
confirm.revokePersonal: Anything still sending this key, such as {{name}}’s scripts, is refused from its next call. It stays in the list as revoked and can’t be turned back on.
confirm.disable: Its tokens are refused at once and it can’t get new ones. It can’t be turned back on: to restore access, create a new machine identity.
confirm.suspend: Its tokens are refused until you resume it, and it can’t get new ones. {{name}} stays its sponsor.
confirm.delete: Its tokens are refused from their next call and it leaves the list for good. Its audit history stays. To stop it for now, suspend it instead.

title.all: Nothing calls Qeet ID on its own yet

description.all: Give a service a machine identity, a script an API key, or an AI agent its own credentials.
description.key: A key lets a script or CI job call the Qeet ID API. For a service, a machine identity’s short-lived tokens are safer.
description.identity: A machine identity lets a service get short-lived tokens with a client ID and secret.
description.agent: An agent acts within its scopes for the person who sponsors it, with tokens that last minutes.

empty.filteredDescription: Try other filters, or clear them to see everything.

keyDrawer.title: New API key
keyDrawer.description: The key is shown once, when it’s made.
keyDrawer.replaceDescription: A new key with the same scopes. Qeet ID has no rotate, so revoke the old key once nothing uses it.
keyDrawer.name: Name
keyDrawer.scopesHelp: What the key can do. Choose the fewest it needs: with none, it can call nothing.
keyDrawer.neverHelp: It works until someone revokes it
keyDrawer.missingTitle: The key was made, but its secret didn’t arrive
keyDrawer.missing: It can never be used. Revoke it and make another.
keyDrawer.thenRevokeHint: Once everything uses the new key, revoke the old one from the list: until then both work.

identityDrawer.title: New machine identity
identityDrawer.description: Its client secret is shown once, when it’s made.
identityDrawer.name: Name
identityDrawer.scopesHelp: What its tokens can do. Choose the fewest it needs.

agentDrawer.title: New agent
agentDrawer.description: Its secret is shown once, when it’s made.
agentDrawer.name: Name
agentDrawer.scopesHelp: What its tokens can do, including the secrets it may read (vault:).
agentDrawer.sponsorHelp: The person who answers for it. You can transfer it later.

transfer.title: Transfer sponsorship
transfer.description: Moves every agent one person sponsors to another, in one step.
transfer.previewList: {{names}}. {{name}} answers for them from now on; moving them back is another transfer.

chooseKind.title: New credential
chooseKind.description: What will use it decides the kind.
chooseKind.label: What will use it
chooseKind.identityHelp: A machine identity: it trades a client secret for tokens that expire within minutes.
chooseKind.keyHelp: An API key: one static key, the simplest to set up. It works until it expires or is revoked.
chooseKind.agentHelp: An agent: a person sponsors it, its tokens last an hour at most, and every agent can be suspended at once.

unmanaged.title: Unmanaged AI clients
unmanaged.note: Applications that can act for a person through a token-exchange grant and aren’t registered here. Review each: register it as an agent, or mark it reviewed.
unmanaged.none: None found: every application with a token-exchange grant has been reviewed.

suspendAll.title: Suspend every agent
suspendAll.note_one: For an agent misbehaving when you don’t know which. The {{n}} active agent stops at once: its tokens are refused, and it gets no new one until you resume it.
suspendAll.note_other: For an agent misbehaving when you don’t know which. The {{n}} active agents stop at once: their tokens are refused, and none gets a new one until you resume it.
suspendAll.confirm: Their tokens are refused at once and none gets a new one. You resume them one at a time.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Encrypted vault for the keys your services and agents read, such as a Stripe or Slack token. Lists never show a value; each reveal is written to the audit log.
secrets.shortHint: Under 8 characters: too short to show its end

band.growthLabel: Secrets added in the last {{months}} months

reveal.recorded: Revealed just now by {{name}}. The audit log records it.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: Services and agents that read vault:{{name}} get nothing from their next read, and the value is gone for good.

empty.title: No secrets yet
empty.description: Store a key your services or agents need, and they read it with a vault: scope instead of keeping it themselves.

secretDrawer.title: New secret
secretDrawer.description: Encrypted as soon as it’s saved.
secretDrawer.name: Name
secretDrawer.nameReadAs: Read as vault:{{name}}. It can’t change once saved.
secretDrawer.nameTaken: A secret has this name already.
secretDrawer.scopeHelp: A label that groups it with others. It doesn’t limit who can read it.
secretDrawer.valueHelp: After saving, only a reveal shows it.

rotateSecret.title: Rotate {{name}}
rotateSecret.neverChanged: Never changed since it was added
rotateSecret.warningTitle: The old value is gone when you save
rotateSecret.warning: Qeet ID keeps no copy, so anything still using the old value of {{name}} fails. Update it at its source first.
rotateSecret.valueHelp: Hidden as you type. After saving, only a reveal shows it.

signingKeys.title: Signing keys
signingKeys.description: They sign every access token, ID token and verifiable credential Qeet ID issues. One key set serves every organisation.
signingKeys.stagesNote: A key is published before it signs and stays published after, so apps always hold the key a token needs. Rotation runs in the deployment, not from the console.

does.candidate: Published in the key set so apps can cache it. It signs nothing yet.
does.active: Signs every new token. There is only ever one.
does.retired: Signs nothing. Still published, so tokens it signed keep verifying until it leaves the set.

empty.title: No signing keys published
empty.description: The deployment has no key in its key set: no token can be signed or checked.

credentials.title: Verifiable credentials
credentials.description: Signed statements about people, such as their employment, that anyone can check against Qeet ID’s public keys.
credentials.search: Search by subject, type or ID

band.growthLabel: Credentials issued in the last {{months}} months

revoke.title: Revoke this {{type}}?
revoke.description: Anyone who checks it from then on is told it’s revoked, though {{subject}} still holds it. It can’t be undone.

empty.title: No credentials issued yet
empty.description: Issue one to give a person a signed statement, such as their employment, that others can check.

issue.title: Issue a credential
issue.description: Signed with the active signing key and shown once, to give to the person.
issue.subject: Subject
issue.subjectHelp: Who it’s about: their user ID, email or DID.
issue.typeHelp: What kind of statement it is.
issue.claimsHelp: A JSON object: what the credential states.
issue.claimsInvalid: Enter a JSON object, such as {"employeeId": "QEE-1041"}.

verify.title: Verify a credential
verify.description: The check anyone can run: its signature, its expiry, and whether it’s been revoked.
verify.validWhy: Signed by Qeet ID, not expired and not revoked.

reason.signature_invalid: Its signature doesn’t check out, or it has expired.
reason.unknown: Qeet ID has no record of issuing it.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Qeet ID posts each event, signed, to these endpoints, and retries a failed one for about 2 days.

line.overlap: New signing secret · the old one stops {{when}}

confirm.disable: Events that happen while it’s off aren’t sent, now or later. Deliveries already waiting are held and go out when you enable it.
confirm.rotate: You get a new secret, shown once. For 24 hours each delivery carries both signatures, so the endpoint can switch without missing one; rotating again in that time ends the older secret at once.

rotated.title: New signing secret for {{host}}
rotated.description: The previous secret also signs each delivery until {{date}}.

empty.title: No webhooks yet
empty.description: Add an endpoint to get people, group and session changes as they happen.

webhookDrawer.title: New webhook
webhookDrawer.description: Qeet ID posts a signed JSON event to the endpoint for each event you pick. Neither can change later.
webhookDrawer.urlHelp: A public https address. It must answer 2xx within 10 seconds; a failed delivery is retried for about 2 days.
webhookDrawer.urlInvalid: Enter a full URL, starting https://.

webhook.notFoundDescription: It may belong to another organisation, or the link is wrong.

band.deliveredNote: {{n}} of the last {{total}}, {{first}} on the first try
band.gaveUpNote: After {{max}} tries, or a refusal it won’t retry

notice.autoTitle: Turned off on {{date}} after 3 days of failed deliveries
notice.failing: Each delivery is retried for about 2 days. If it still fails, the webhook turns off at its first failure after {{date}}.
notice.overlap: The previous secret also signs each delivery until {{when}}. Switch the endpoint to the new one before then.
notice.auto_zero: Nothing is waiting to go out; {{gaveUp}} gave up. Fix the endpoint first, then enable it and retry those.
notice.auto_one: {{held}} delivery is held and goes out when you enable it; {{gaveUp}} gave up. Fix the endpoint first, then enable it and retry those.
notice.auto_other: {{held}} deliveries are held and go out when you enable it; {{gaveUp}} gave up. Fix the endpoint first, then enable it and retry those.
notice.disabled_zero: Events that happen while it’s off aren’t sent, now or later.
notice.disabled_one: Events that happen while it’s off aren’t sent, now or later. {{held}} held delivery goes out when you enable it.
notice.disabled_other: Events that happen while it’s off aren’t sent, now or later. {{held}} held deliveries go out when you enable it.

health.title: Deliveries over time
health.note: The recent deliveries by when they were made. A failed one is retried with growing gaps, up to 60 times over about 2 days; a refusal (4xx, other than 408 and 429) isn’t retried.
health.none: Nothing sent yet: test it to see a delivery here.

deliveries.title: Recent deliveries
deliveries.note: Newest first. Open one for its request and the endpoint’s answer.
deliveries.noteLimit: The last {{n}}, newest first. Open one for its request and the endpoint’s answer.
deliveries.noneOff: No deliveries. While it’s off, events aren’t sent.

events.title: Events it gets
events.note: To change them, create a new webhook: Qeet ID can’t change a webhook’s events or address.
events.undescribed: An event this console doesn’t describe yet.

secret.title: Signing secret
secret.note: Each delivery is signed with it, so the endpoint can tell it came from Qeet ID.
secret.currentNote: Shown once, when it was made or rotated.
secret.overlapLabel: The previous secret stops signing on {{when}}
secret.previousNote: Both secrets sign each delivery until {{when}}, so the endpoint can switch without missing one.
secret.noneNote: After a rotation, the old secret signs for 24 hours too.

signature.name: X-Qeet-Signature
signature.what: "sha256=" and the HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a dot and the body. Two, comma-separated, while a previous secret still signs.

timestamp.name: X-Qeet-Timestamp
timestamp.what: When this attempt was signed, in Unix seconds. Reject old ones.

delivery.name: X-Qeet-Delivery-ID
delivery.what: The same on every retry, so the endpoint can ignore a repeat.

delivery.usedUpNote: A retry doesn’t reset the count: if it fails again it gives up at once. Fix the endpoint first.
delivery.noBody: The endpoint answered with no body.
delivery.notReached: No response: the endpoint wasn’t reached.

authHooks.title: Auth hooks
authHooks.description: On every sign-in, whatever the method, Qeet ID asks each hook that’s on to allow or deny it once the first factor is proven. It waits {{seconds}} seconds for each.

band.waitNote: Hooks run in turn, each waiting up to {{seconds}} seconds: what a sign-in waits when all are slow.

row.allowsLine: An outage at its end never locks people out
row.blocksLine: If it’s down or slow, nobody can sign in

actions.allowHint: An outage never locks people out

confirm.off: Sign-ins stop waiting for it and nothing it would deny is denied, until you turn it back on.
confirm.block: If it’s down, takes over 3 seconds or answers with an error, nobody can sign in until it’s back.
confirm.remove: Sign-ins stop waiting for it and nothing it would deny is denied. Its secret goes with it; adding it back needs a new one.

empty.title: No auth hooks
empty.description: Add one to let your own policy allow or deny each sign-in.

call.title: What a hook gets and answers
call.note: Qeet ID posts this JSON and reads the answer within 3 seconds. Hooks run oldest first; the first deny stops the sign-in.
call.signature: Each call carries X-Qeet-Signature: "sha256=" and the HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the hook’s secret.
call.deny: "decision": "deny" blocks the sign-in, with your "message" if you give one; anything else allows it.
call.claims: "claims" are added to the person’s access token under "claims", and kept when it’s refreshed.

hookDrawer.title: Add auth hook
hookDrawer.description: It runs on every sign-in once it’s added.
hookDrawer.urlHelp: A public https address that answers within {{seconds}} seconds.
hookDrawer.secretHelp: Yours: each call is signed with it. It can’t be shown again.
hookDrawer.allowHelp: An outage at your end never locks people out. Each skipped check is recorded in Activity.
hookDrawer.blockHelp: For strict policies. If your endpoint is down or slow, nobody can sign in.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The addresses and keys your integrations work with.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.note: Every SDK finds the rest from the issuer.

issuer.label: Issuer
issuer.what: Where SDKs and apps start: its discovery document lists the rest.

discovery.label: Discovery
discovery.what: The OpenID configuration: endpoints, scopes and algorithms.

jwks.label: JWKS
jwks.what: The public keys that check tokens and credentials.

token.label: Machine tokens
token.what: Where machine identities trade a client secret for a token.

agentToken.label: Agent tokens
agentToken.what: Where agents trade their secret for a token.

verify.label: Credential check
verify.what: Where anyone verifies a credential Qeet ID issued.

keys.title: Signing keys
keys.note_one: {{n}} key published in the key set.
keys.note_other: {{n}} keys published in the key set.

health.title: Service health
health.note: Qeet ID reports no health to an organisation. Running it yourself? Its /readyz endpoint and its metrics feed your own monitoring.

bots.title: Bots
bots.description: Automations that react to identity events.

empty.title: Bots aren’t available yet
empty.description: Until they are, webhooks send identity events to your own code, and auth hooks run it during sign-in.
